 Judgment
The petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained during road
traffic accident.
2. Petition averments in brief are as follows; That on 23.03.2022 at about 05.30 P

.M., while the petitioner was crossing inner ring road, was hit by the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-ED-3795,
Augsta Nandan vs M.Daniel Paul on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50631153/
1 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner.
That the petitioner was taken to St.John's Hospital and was admitted as an inpatient.
That the petitioner was working as House maid at Military camp, Bangalore and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month and lost income and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
Thus prays to grant compensation as sought for.

3. Per contra, the respondent No.2 filed the written statement denies the negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler and for other objections has sought for dismissal of the petition against the respondent.
4. On the basis of the Pleadings and materials, the following issues were framed.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred 23.03.2022 at about 05.30 PM., while crossing the inner ring road, opposite to Military Quarters,
Bangalore, which was due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-ED-3795 by its driver ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.
What order
or award?
5. In order to substantiate the allegation, the petitioner got examined herself as PW-1 and two witnesses were examined as PW-2 and PW-3 and has produced 24 documents on his behalf.
The respondent did not lead any evidence.

6. Heard from the counsel for the petitioner and the respondent No.2.
7.

My findings on the above points are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  8. Point No.1: According to the petitioner, on 23.03.2022 at about 05.30 P.M., while the petitioner was crossing inner ring road, was hit by the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-ED-3795, riden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner.
That the petitioner was taken to St.John's Hospital and was admitted as an inpatient.
That the petitioner was working as House maid at Military camp, Bangalore and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

That Augsta Nandan vs M.Daniel Paul on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50631153/
2 she has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food and nourishment and etc., That due to the accident, she has lost income and she was only earning member in the family.
That she is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
That a case in Cr.No.20/2022 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle.
Thus prays to grant compensation as sought for.
9. In order to substantiate the allegation, the petitioner got examined herself as PW-1 and two witnesses were examined as PW-2 and PW-3 and has produced 24 documents on his behalf.
The respondent did not lead any evidence.

To further prove the case, the petitioner has produced copy of FIS as Ex.P.2, lodged by herself on 25.03.2022, she submits in the FIS that on 23.03.2022 at about 05.30 PM., while she along with her daughter and grand son came from Egipura in the autorickshaw and wanted to enter the military camp, was crossing the road, while the offending vehicle i.e., super splender bearing No.KA- 01-ED-3795 came from Dommulur to Egipura, ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, in a haphazard manner in the road and caused the accident.
That she being injured was taken to St.John's hospital immediately and was shifted to Bowring and Lady curzon Hospital for further treatment.

The statement was recorded by the police Head constable No.10643 in Bowring and Lady curzon Hospital and has lodged FIR which is as per Ex.P.1 in Cr.No.20/2022,
alleging offences punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC.
That the spot panchanama is produced as Ex.P.3 and the sketch as Ex.P.3(a), showing the place of accident.
As per the said sketch, the accident has occurred in the middle of the road,where the road is shown to be of 33 feet and the place of accident is at about 20 feet from center median.

The MVA report is produced as Ex.P.4 showing the head lamp, front wheel assembly, handle bar, crash guard damaged at right side and the opinion is given that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects.
10. The wound certificate is issued by the Bowring and Lady curzon Hospital.
A notice is issued to the owner of the vehicle as required under section 133 of IMV Act, as per Ex.P.6.

There is reply by the owner to the said notice, marked as Ex.P.7, giving the details of the ownership of the vehicle,
along with the details of the rider of the vehicle and the details of the driving license pertaining to the said rider along with policy number of the vehicle.

The final report is produced as per Ex.P.8,
alleging the offences punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC.
11.
The defence was taken up that there is negligence on the part of the petitioner in causing the accident.
That there is delay in filing of the complaint and thus, denies that the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the two wheeler.
Therefore with the said defence, the PW-1 was cross examined by the counsel for the respondent.
But the important fact is that the respondent did not lead any evidence inspite of providing sufficient opportunity.
12. The PW-1 submits that she has given statement before police, which is considered as FIS.
She has also submitted that her son has seen the accident.
She further submits that since she was under the treatment, she could not lodge complaint immediately as on the date of accident.
As per FIS, the statement was taken i.e.,of the petitioner in the Bowring and Lady curzon Hospital.
This clearly goes to show that the petitioner immediately after the accident was admitted to the hospital.
As per the petitioner, she was admitted to St.John's hospital immediately after the accident.
She has produced some medical bills/ invoices showing that she has spent some amount in the said St.John's medical college hospital on 23.03.2022.

The medical record technician of Bowring and Lady curzon Augsta Nandan vs M.Daniel Paul on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50631153/
3
Hospital, Shivajinagar was summoned to produce the case sheet and inpatient records and was examined as PW-3.
He has produced the MLC as Ex.P.21.

As per register, reference of the St.John's hospital is also noted and history of RTA is shown as near Halasur police station and as hit by the two wheeler at 05.30 PM., by the vehicle bearing No.KA-01-ED-9785.
This MLC was prepared on 24.10.2022 at 01.00 PM.
The police intimation is also sent as per Ex.P.22 which clearly shows the date and time of the accident.

When ever any person is admitted to hospital, and especially in the cases of accident, it is the bounden duty of concerned hospital to immediately intimate to the nearest police station regarding the accident and prepare the MLC.
But why the said authorities of the St.John's hospital have not prepared the MLC is not known.
However the MLC are prepared by the Bowring and Lady curzon Hospital immediately as and when the petitioner was brought to the hospital i.e., on the next day of the accident.
Therefore when she was under treatment, the police official have recorded the statement of the petitioner in the hospital.
The document are very much clear that the accident occurred 23.03.2022.
Therefore the delay in lodging of FIR can be condoned for the purpose of this case.
13. Further the question was posed to the PW-1 with regard to her negligence in crossing the road.
As per the said sketch the place of accident is shown at a distance of nearly 20 feet from divider.
She submits that there was zebra signal.

Though it was argued that there was no signal to cross the road,
the respondent did not make any effort to prove the same before the court.
However, the fact is that the petitioner had already crossed about 20 feet from the median and there was only small space left to reach the road, i.e., of 13 feet.
Therefore it was the rider of offending vehicle, who ought to had seen the on going vehicles or pedestrian etc.
If the rider of offending vehicle was not rash or negligent, would have applied the brake immediately as and when he saw the petitioners and her family member crossing the road.
The MVA report is given that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
It clearly shows that the rider of the two wheeler was rash and negligent in crossing the road.
Rider of the offending vehicle was not summoned before this court.
However, the owner by giving reply to the notice issued to the police, has clearly submitted that one Sri.Mathew Morris Paul.D, aged 22 years was riding the vehicle.
14. The counsel for the respondent urges that the petitioner ought to had taken care of while crossing the road and thus the contributory negligence can be considered.

In this regard the authority in A.Anandan Vs Abdul Azeez and others reported in 2004 ACJ 1091, of High court of Karnataka, where discussing the fact that the pedestrian sustained injuries by the motor cyclist, and neither the motor cyclist nor any other evidence was produced by the respondent, held that the motor cyclist was solely responsible for the accident.

entities.text: A.Anandan Vs Abdul Azeez and others reported in 2004 ACJ 1091
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This judgment is aptly applicable to the instant case, since the motor cyclist has hit the petitioner, and who has failed to put his appearance and give proper evidence.

Therefore by all these evidence on record where the petitioner has already crossed the road and covered more than half of the road and no evidence is lead to rebut the same, this court based upon the oral and documentary evidence lead supported by the charge sheet, which is against rider of the two wheeler, can easily come to the conclusion there is negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle and thus the above point is answered in affirmative.
15. Point No.2: The petitioner in order to show her age, has produced the copy of the adhaar card as Ex.P.9, where the petitioner is shown to be born in the year 1970.

Thus the petitioner's age as on Augsta Nandan vs M.Daniel Paul on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50631153/
4 date of accident, is 52 years and appropriate multiplier for the said age is 11.

sentences.text: what is the future loss of income for the petitioner is to be seen.
16. The petitioner submits that she was working as cook, maid in the military camp.
That she has lost income due to the said accident and injuries caused.
Therefore submits that she has disability and in this regard she got examined one Dr.Nagaraj, the orthopedic surgeon as PW-2.
But she has not produced any document to show that she was working as cook/maid in the military camp and therefore notional income to an extent of Rs.14,750/- can be considered.
17. As per the PW-2, the petitioner as on 21.11.2022, has wasting of the left thigh muscles, restricted left knee and ankle movements.
Thus after examination has assessed the total physical disability of left lower limb as 42% and the whole body disability of 14%.
He has produced the clinical examination report as Ex.P.18 and X-ray as Ex.P.19.
During his cross examination he submits that the implants are in situ and the petitioner is advised to get removal of implants.
Denies all the other suggestions made by the counsel for the respondent with regard to the verocity of the affidavit filed by the petitioner.
Apart from this, there is nothing on record to disbelieve the verocity of the PW-2 who is an orthopedic surgeon.
Therefore the whole body disability to an extent of 14% can be considered.
18. As per the available materials on record, Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.17, the medical expenses would tune to Rs.24,348/- , which can be rounded of to Rs.24,500/-as medical expenses and hospital charges.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for Rs.24,500/- under the head of medical expenses and hospital charges.
19. The petitioner has undergone CRIF with ILN tibia (9X34), arm-sling for lateral clavicle and SAS on 26.03.2022.
The PW-2 deposes that the petitioner has undergone fracture of left leg both bones fracture.
That the implants are inside the body and requires removal for which the PW-2 submits that another surgery is required, which cost about Rs.60,000/-.
But however same may be reduced in the other hospitals and therefore an amount of Rs.20,000/- can be granted for removal of implants.

20. As per the Wound Certificate and discharge summary produced as Ex.P.5 and P.12, the petitioner had sustained fracture of laceration 5X2 on left temporal region, swelling near left side of clavicle, left lower limbs swelling and abnormal mobility, displaced of 1/3 rd left clavicle, displaced of upper 1/3rd left shaft of tibia, segmental displacement of upper, lower shaft of tibia, displaced disatal 1/3rd of fibula, which are grievous in nature.
The petitioner was hospitalized from 24.03.2022 to 28.03.2022.
Thus she was in the hospital as inpatient for 5 days and may be expected to be in the complete bed rest for two months.
The clinical examination report and X-ray are also produced as Ex.P.18 and P.19 by the PW-2.

Thus the petitioner can be made entitled for Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.5,000/- towards food and nourishment charges,
Rs.3,000/- towards conveyance charges, and Rs.5,000/- towards attendant charges and Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Augsta Nandan vs M.Daniel Paul on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50631153/
5 21.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for reasonable compensation as under:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/- 2 Medical expenses and hospital charges Rs.24,500/- 3 Food and nourishment Rs.5,000/- 4 Conveyance charges Rs.3,000/- 5 Attendant charges Rs.5,000/- 6 Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/- 7
Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/- 8 Loss of income during laid up period Rs.29,500/- 9 Loss of future income Rs.2,72,580/-

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,34,580/-, which can be rounded to Rs.4,35,000/-.
22.
In this case, there is no disputed fact that the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-ED-3795 which caused the accident.
The respondent no.2 has failed to prove that the insurance company is not liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount and as on the date of accident the insurance policy was in force.
Hence, this issue is answered accordingly burdening the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner, along with the present Bank rate of interest at 6%.
23. Point No.3:

For the reasons stated in the aforesaid paragraphs, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,35,000/- with interest at 6%
per annum (excluding Future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of realization of the entire amount.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within two months from the date of judgment.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.5,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

(Sharmila C.S) V ASCJ & Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru.
